14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]

407: \```

415: │     └─ Expected outcome A

417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B

426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
428: 
429: **Format**:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

21: 
22: ### Location & Naming

25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95:

98: ```markdown

100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes

109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

245: - Root cause analysis required

253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

40: 
41: ### Live Decision Model
42: 
43: Convergence decides whether the loop should continue, recover from a stuck state, or stop. A STOP candidate is not legal until the legal-stop gate bundle passes. Novelty math can nominate STOP; gates authorize it.
44: 
45: The live deep-research algorithm evaluates:
46: 
47: | Stage | Outcome |
48: |-------|---------|
49: | Hard stop and completion candidate | Stop unconditionally on max iterations; nominate STOP when all key questions are answered |
50: | Stuck detection | Enter recovery after configured consecutive no-progress iterations |
51: | Composite convergence | Nominate STOP when weighted signal score is above `0.60` |
52: | Legal-stop gates | Allow or block the STOP candidate |
53: | Graph gates | Add STOP-blocking graph checks when `graphEvents` exist |
54: 
55: ### Convergence Modes
56: 
57: The shared convergence runtime accepts four values. The workflow keeps hard terminal boundaries outside mode-specific convergence handling.
58: 
59: | Mode | Live Behavior |
60: |------|---------------|
61: | `default` | Uses the normal full-history convergence signals and sends a legal STOP to synthesis. This is the fallback when no mode is supplied. |
62: | `off` | Skips convergence-driven STOP candidates. Max iterations, pause or cancellation, manual stop, recovery halt, and unrecoverable error behavior remain active. |
63: | `sliding-window` | Uses a bounded graph-novelty window, defaulting to 5 snapshots, while preserving the ordinary legal-stop and synthesis path. |
64: | `divergent` | Computes convergence normally, but translates an eligible legal STOP into a three-seat direction-selection pivot and continues from the selected focus. |
65: 
66: #### Divergent Pivot Contract
67: 
68: Research pivots are eligible only when the workflow decision is `STOP` and the exact internal reason is `composite_converged` or `all_questions_answered`. The legal-stop and quality gates run before this branch. `maxIterationsReached`, `blockedStop`, `stuckRecovery`, `minIterationsNotReached`, `error`, `manualStop`, and `userPaused` are explicitly excluded. Max iterations, pause or cancellation, manual stop, and unrecoverable error therefore never dispatch a pivot Council.
69: 
70: Each eligible pivot runs one native, in-process Council round with exactly three distinct seats: analytical, critical, and pragmatic. It does not use an external CLI. The transaction requires all three seat returns to be parse-valid and at least two seats to materially endorse the same candidate without a high-severity blocker. Research candidates come from persisted adjacent questions, contradiction or verification gaps, missing source classes, alternate evidence methods, and independent checks of recent findings. A completed pivot restores the selected candidate's focus and returns to the research loop; a failed pivot fails closed to synthesis.
71: 
72: Every pivot dispatches three seats, so a run that pivots has proportionally higher model cost and duration than the same run under `default`, `off`, or `sliding-window`. Pivot evidence is isolated under `<artifactRoot>/divergent/pivots/<pivotId>/council/**`, including config, append-only state, three seat artifacts, deliberation, and report. This path is distinct from ordinary planning Council artifacts under a spec packet's `ai-council/**` tree.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 2. STOP CONTRACT
77: 
78: ### stopReason Values
79: 
80: | Value | When It Is Used |
81: |-------|-----------------|
82: | `converged` | Legal-stop gates passed and the loop may exit normally |
83: | `maxIterationsReached` | The loop hit the configured iteration cap |
84: | `userPaused` | A pause sentinel or equivalent user pause request halted execution |
85: | `blockedStop` | A STOP candidate was blocked by legal-stop or graph gates |
86: | `stuckRecovery` | Stuck detection triggered or failed recovery |
87: | `error` | The loop hit an unrecoverable workflow or state error |
88: 
89: ### Legacy Stop Labels
90: 
91: Legacy labels are normalized before persistence:
92: 
93: | Legacy label or phrase | New `stopReason` |
94: |------------------------|------------------|
95: | `composite_converged` | `converged` |
96: | `novelty below threshold` | `converged` |
97: | `all_questions_answered` | `converged` |
98: | `max_iterations_reached` | `maxIterationsReached` |
99: | `paused` | `userPaused` |
100: | `stuck_detected` | `stuckRecovery` |
101: | `stuck_unrecoverable` | `stuckRecovery` |
102: 
103: ---
104: 
105: ## 3. LIVE ALGORITHM
106: 
107: ### Decision Order
108: 
109: ```text
110: 1. If iteration count >= maxIterations, STOP with maxIterationsReached.
111: 2. If all key questions have evidence-backed answers, nominate STOP.
112: 3. If stuckCount >= stuckThreshold, enter stuck recovery.
113: 4. Compute composite convergence signals.
114: 5. If weighted stop score > 0.60, nominate STOP.
115: 6. Evaluate legal-stop gates for every STOP candidate except hard max-iteration stop.
116: 7. If graphEvents exist, evaluate graph-aware STOP blockers.
117: 8. If gates pass, pivot for an eligible divergent reason or STOP normally; otherwise emit blockedStop and CONTINUE with recovery focus.
118: ```
119: 
120: ### Composite Signal Weights
121: 
122: | Signal | Weight | Min Iterations | Measures |
123: |--------|--------|----------------|----------|
124: | Rolling Average | `0.30` | 3 evidence iterations | Recent information yield |
125: | MAD Noise Floor | `0.35` | 4 evidence iterations | Signal vs noise in `newInfoRatio` |
126: | Question Entropy | `0.35` | 1 key question | Evidence-backed question coverage |
127: 
128: The weighted stop score is normalized over active signals. STOP is nominated only when the normalized score is greater than `0.60`. See `convergence-signals.md` for exact signal rules and reporting.
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## 4. LEGAL STOP GATES
133: 
134: Every non-terminal STOP candidate must pass the gate bundle before the workflow exits.
135: 
136: | Gate | Rule | Failure |
137: |------|------|---------|
138: | Convergence Gate | Low novelty holds for the required consecutive evidence iterations | Emit `blocked_stop`, continue |
139: | Coverage Gate | Every key question has an evidence-backed answer | Emit `blocked_stop`, continue |
140: | Quality Gate | Source diversity, focus alignment, and no single weak-source dominance pass | Emit `blocked_stop`, continue |
141: | Graph Gate | When graph data exists, graph coverage has no STOP blockers | Emit `graph_convergence`/`blocked_stop`, continue |
142: 
143: The reducer surfaces legal-stop evidence through the findings registry and dashboard. The JSONL event shapes live in `../state/state-jsonl.md`.

148: 
149: | Resource | Use When |
150: |----------|----------|
151: | `convergence-signals.md` | Need scoring, `newInfoRatio`, `stuckCount`, MAD, entropy, report fields, or threshold tuning |
152: | `convergence-recovery.md` | Need stuck recovery, recovery strategy selection, tiered errors, or escalation behavior |
153: | `convergence-graph.md` | Need graph-aware STOP gates, graph convergence events, or coverage graph fallback behavior |
154: | `convergence-reference-only.md` | Need future/reference-only models such as segment filtering, semantic convergence, or optimizer metadata |
155: | `../state/state-jsonl.md` | Need JSONL event shapes persisted by the convergence workflow |
156: | `../state/state-reducer-registry.md` | Need reducer-owned registry/dashboard fields derived from convergence |
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: ## 6. NON-GOALS
161: 
162: - Do not copy `deep-review` convergence into this skill. Use the `deep-review` references for severity-weighted review convergence.
163: - Do not treat reference-only semantic or segment models as executable contracts.
164: - Do not change the YAML workflow by editing this document. This document describes and routes the live contract; workflow changes require command/YAML work.

17: # Convergence Signals Reference
18: 
19: This reference defines the live deep-research convergence signals. The compact stop contract lives in `convergence.md`.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: Define the live convergence signals, scoring rules, threshold semantics, and reporting shape used by deep-research loops.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: Load this reference when calculating `newInfoRatio`, explaining a composite STOP vote, debugging stuck counts, or validating convergence dashboards.
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: Signals nominate STOP; legal-stop and graph gates authorize or block it.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. SIGNAL MODEL
40: 
41: The live model uses three weighted signals and normalizes by the weight of the signals that have enough data to run.
42: 
43: | Signal | Weight | Requires | STOP Vote |
44: |--------|--------|----------|-----------|
45: | Rolling Average | `0.30` | 3 evidence iterations | Average of last 3 `newInfoRatio` values is below `convergenceThreshold` |
46: | MAD Noise Floor | `0.35` | 4 evidence iterations | Latest `newInfoRatio` is at or below `MAD * 1.4826` |
47: | Question Entropy | `0.35` | At least 1 key question | Evidence-backed coverage is at least `0.85` |
48: 
49: `thought` iterations are excluded from rolling average, MAD, and stuck counting because they are analytical-only. `insight` iterations are included in convergence signals but do not count as stuck.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 3. NEW INFO RATIO
54: 
55: `newInfoRatio` measures how much an iteration added relative to accumulated research knowledge.
56: 
57: | Ratio | Meaning |
58: |-------|---------|
59: | `1.0` | Mostly new findings or first broad pass |
60: | `0.7` | Several new findings plus some refinements |
61: | `0.5` | Mixed new and repeated material |
62: | `0.2` | Mostly confirmation or marginal novelty |
63: | `0.0` | No new information |
64: 
65: Agent assessment guidance:
66: 
67: - Fully new finding: count as `1.0`.
68: - Refinement of known finding: count as partial novelty.
69: - Ruled-out direction: count as valuable negative knowledge when it removes a plausible path.
70: - Tentative single-source finding: contribute less than verified or multi-source evidence.
71: - Simplicity bonus may add up to `0.10`, capped at `1.0`, when an iteration materially reduces the search space.
72: 
73: Every iteration record should include `newInfoRatio` and `noveltyJustification`; see `../state/state-jsonl.md`.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 4. STUCK COUNT
78: 
79: `stuckCount` is consecutive no-progress evidence iterations.
80: 
81: ```text
82: for each iteration from newest to oldest:
83:   skip status == "thought"
84:   stop counting when status == "insight"
85:   count if status == "stuck" or newInfoRatio <= noProgressThreshold
86:   stop counting on any productive evidence iteration
87: ```
88: 
89: Default threshold behavior:
90: 
91: - `stuckThreshold`: `3`
92: - `noProgressThreshold`: implementation default aligned with the workflow's recovery check
93: - Recovery route: `convergence-recovery.md`
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 5. ROLLING AVERAGE
98: 
99: Rolling average uses the last three evidence iterations.
100: 
101: ```text
102: evidenceIterations = iterations where status != "thought"
103: recent = last 3 evidenceIterations
104: rollingAvg = mean(recent.newInfoRatio)
105: rollingStop = rollingAvg < convergenceThreshold
106: ```
107: 
108: This signal is unavailable before three evidence iterations. The composite vote normalizes over active signals, so early runs can still use question coverage without pretending the rolling signal exists.
109: 
110: ---
111: 
112: ## 6. MAD NOISE FLOOR
113: 
114: MAD compares the latest ratio against the noise floor in the accumulated evidence ratios.
115: 
116: ```text
117: ratios = evidenceIterations.newInfoRatio
118: medianRatio = median(ratios)
119: mad = median(abs(ratio - medianRatio) for ratio in ratios)
120: noiseFloor = mad * 1.4826
121: madStop = latestEvidenceRatio <= noiseFloor
122: ```
123: 
124: Interpretation:
125: 
126: | Condition | Meaning |
127: |-----------|---------|
128: | Latest ratio above floor | Signal still exceeds observed noise |
129: | Latest ratio within floor | New findings may be indistinguishable from noise |
130: | Very high floor | Iteration quality is unstable; narrow the focus before trusting STOP |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ## 7. QUESTION ENTROPY
135: 
136: Question entropy is evidence-backed key-question coverage.
137: 
138: ```text
139: answered = count(keyQuestions with evidence-backed answers)
140: total = count(keyQuestions)
141: coverage = answered / total
142: entropyStop = coverage >= 0.85
143: ```
144: 
145: Tentative-only findings do not satisfy evidence-backed coverage. Graph events may add extra STOP blockers when graph coverage disagrees with inline question coverage; see `convergence-graph.md`.
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ## 8. COMPOSITE SCORE
150: 
151: ```text
152: activeSignals = signals with enough data
153: stopScore = sum(signal.weight for active STOP votes) / sum(active signal weights)
154: stopCandidate = stopScore > 0.60
155: ```
156: 
157: The score nominates STOP only. `convergence.md` defines the legal-stop gates that decide whether the loop may exit.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 9. REPORTING
162: 
163: Every completed loop should report:
164: 
165: ```text
166: CONVERGENCE REPORT
167: ------------------
168: Stop reason: converged | maxIterationsReached | userPaused | stuckRecovery | error
169: Iterations completed: N
170: Questions answered: X/Y
171: Average newInfoRatio trend: [...]
172: Composite stop score: 0.XX
173: Signals:
174:   Rolling Avg (w=0.30): STOP|CONTINUE
175:   MAD Noise (w=0.35): STOP|CONTINUE
176:   Entropy (w=0.35): STOP|CONTINUE
177: Legal-stop gates: pass|blocked
178: Graph gates: pass|blocked|not_applicable
179: ```
180: 
181: Dashboard and registry fields derived from these signals are documented in `../state/state-reducer-registry.md`.
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ## 10. THRESHOLD TUNING
186: 
187: | Goal | Adjustment |
188: |------|------------|
189: | Deeper research | Lower `convergenceThreshold`, raise `maxIterations` |
190: | Faster completion | Raise `convergenceThreshold`, lower `maxIterations` |
191: | More stuck recovery | Lower `stuckThreshold` cautiously |
192: | Fewer false stops | Keep legal-stop and graph gates enabled |
193: 
194: Optimizer-managed fields are described in `convergence-reference-only.md`. Optimizer proposals are advisory and do not override locked stop-contract fields.

23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: Define the live convergence signals, scoring rules, threshold semantics, and reporting shape used by deep-research loops.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: Load this reference when calculating `newInfoRatio`, explaining a composite STOP vote, debugging stuck counts, or validating convergence dashboards.
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: Signals nominate STOP; legal-stop and graph gates authorize or block it.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. SIGNAL MODEL
40: 
41: The live model uses three weighted signals and normalizes by the weight of the signals that have enough data to run.
42: 
43: | Signal | Weight | Requires | STOP Vote |
44: |--------|--------|----------|-----------|
45: | Rolling Average | `0.30` | 3 evidence iterations | Average of last 3 `newInfoRatio` values is below `convergenceThreshold` |
46: | MAD Noise Floor | `0.35` | 4 evidence iterations | Latest `newInfoRatio` is at or below `MAD * 1.4826` |
47: | Question Entropy | `0.35` | At least 1 key question | Evidence-backed coverage is at least `0.85` |
48: 
49: `thought` iterations are excluded from rolling average, MAD, and stuck counting because they are analytical-only. `insight` iterations are included in convergence signals but do not count as stuck.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 3. NEW INFO RATIO
54: 
55: `newInfoRatio` measures how much an iteration added relative to accumulated research knowledge.
56: 
57: | Ratio | Meaning |
58: |-------|---------|
59: | `1.0` | Mostly new findings or first broad pass |
60: | `0.7` | Several new findings plus some refinements |
61: | `0.5` | Mixed new and repeated material |
62: | `0.2` | Mostly confirmation or marginal novelty |
63: | `0.0` | No new information |
64: 
65: Agent assessment guidance:
66: 
67: - Fully new finding: count as `1.0`.
68: - Refinement of known finding: count as partial novelty.
69: - Ruled-out direction: count as valuable negative knowledge when it removes a plausible path.
70: - Tentative single-source finding: contribute less than verified or multi-source evidence.
71: - Simplicity bonus may add up to `0.10`, capped at `1.0`, when an iteration materially reduces the search space.
72: 
73: Every iteration record should include `newInfoRatio` and `noveltyJustification`; see `../state/state-jsonl.md`.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 4. STUCK COUNT
78: 
79: `stuckCount` is consecutive no-progress evidence iterations.
80: 
81: ```text
82: for each iteration from newest to oldest:
83:   skip status == "thought"
84:   stop counting when status == "insight"
85:   count if status == "stuck" or newInfoRatio <= noProgressThreshold
86:   stop counting on any productive evidence iteration
87: ```
88: 
89: Default threshold behavior:
90: 
91: - `stuckThreshold`: `3`
92: - `noProgressThreshold`: implementation default aligned with the workflow's recovery check
93: - Recovery route: `convergence-recovery.md`
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 5. ROLLING AVERAGE
98: 
99: Rolling average uses the last three evidence iterations.
100: 
101: ```text
102: evidenceIterations = iterations where status != "thought"
103: recent = last 3 evidenceIterations
104: rollingAvg = mean(recent.newInfoRatio)
105: rollingStop = rollingAvg < convergenceThreshold
106: ```
107: 
108: This signal is unavailable before three evidence iterations. The composite vote normalizes over active signals, so early runs can still use question coverage without pretending the rolling signal exists.
109: 
110: ---
111: 
112: ## 6. MAD NOISE FLOOR
113: 
114: MAD compares the latest ratio against the noise floor in the accumulated evidence ratios.
115: 
116: ```text
117: ratios = evidenceIterations.newInfoRatio
118: medianRatio = median(ratios)
119: mad = median(abs(ratio - medianRatio) for ratio in ratios)
120: noiseFloor = mad * 1.4826
121: madStop = latestEvidenceRatio <= noiseFloor
122: ```
123: 
124: Interpretation:
125: 
126: | Condition | Meaning |
127: |-----------|---------|
128: | Latest ratio above floor | Signal still exceeds observed noise |
129: | Latest ratio within floor | New findings may be indistinguishable from noise |
130: | Very high floor | Iteration quality is unstable; narrow the focus before trusting STOP |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ## 7. QUESTION ENTROPY
135: 
136: Question entropy is evidence-backed key-question coverage.
137: 
138: ```text
139: answered = count(keyQuestions with evidence-backed answers)
140: total = count(keyQuestions)
141: coverage = answered / total
142: entropyStop = coverage >= 0.85
143: ```
144: 
145: Tentative-only findings do not satisfy evidence-backed coverage. Graph events may add extra STOP blockers when graph coverage disagrees with inline question coverage; see `convergence-graph.md`.
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ## 8. COMPOSITE SCORE
150: 
151: ```text
152: activeSignals = signals with enough data
153: stopScore = sum(signal.weight for active STOP votes) / sum(active signal weights)
154: stopCandidate = stopScore > 0.60
155: ```
156: 
157: The score nominates STOP only. `convergence.md` defines the legal-stop gates that decide whether the loop may exit.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 9. REPORTING
162: 
163: Every completed loop should report:
164: 
165: ```text
166: CONVERGENCE REPORT
167: ------------------
168: Stop reason: converged | maxIterationsReached | userPaused | stuckRecovery | error
169: Iterations completed: N
170: Questions answered: X/Y
171: Average newInfoRatio trend: [...]
172: Composite stop score: 0.XX
173: Signals:
174:   Rolling Avg (w=0.30): STOP|CONTINUE
175:   MAD Noise (w=0.35): STOP|CONTINUE
176:   Entropy (w=0.35): STOP|CONTINUE
177: Legal-stop gates: pass|blocked
178: Graph gates: pass|blocked|not_applicable
179: ```
180: 
181: Dashboard and registry fields derived from these signals are documented in `../state/state-reducer-registry.md`.
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ## 10. THRESHOLD TUNING
186: 
187: | Goal | Adjustment |
188: |------|------------|
189: | Deeper research | Lower `convergenceThreshold`, raise `maxIterations` |
190: | Faster completion | Raise `convergenceThreshold`, lower `maxIterations` |
191: | More stuck recovery | Lower `stuckThreshold` cautiously |
192: | Fewer false stops | Keep legal-stop and graph gates enabled |
193: 
194: Optimizer-managed fields are described in `convergence-reference-only.md`. Optimizer proposals are advisory and do not override locked stop-contract fields.

35: ## 2. COMMANDS
36: 
37: | Command | Description |
38: |---------|-------------|
39: | `/deep:research:auto "topic"` | Run autonomous deep research (no approval gates) |
40: | `/deep:research:confirm "topic"` | Run with approval gates at each iteration |
41: | `/deep:research "topic"` | Ask which mode to use |

44: 
45: | Parameter | Default | Description |
46: |-----------|---------|-------------|
47: | `--max-iterations` | 10 | Maximum loop iterations |
48: | `--convergence` | 0.05 | Stop when avg newInfoRatio below this |
49: | `--spec-folder` | auto | Target spec folder path |
50: | `progressiveSynthesis` | true | Allow incremental `research/research.md` updates before final synthesis |
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 3. WHEN TO USE
55: 
56: | Scenario | Use |
57: |----------|-----|
58: | Deep unknown topic, multi-round needed | `/deep:research` |
59: | Simple question, 1-2 sources | Direct search with `@context` |
60: | Check prior work only | The continuity ladder, then the ripgrep recipes in `retrieval-conventions.md` |
61: | Exhaustive critical research | `/deep:research --max-iterations 15 --convergence 0.02` |
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 4. ARCHITECTURE
66: 
67: ```text
68: /deep:research  -->  YAML workflow  -->  @deep-research agent (LEAF)
69:     |                    |                      |
70:     |                    |                      +-- Read state
71:     |                    |                      +-- Research (3-5 actions)
72:     |                    |                      +-- Write findings
73:     |                    |                      +-- Update state
74:     |                    |
75:     |                    +-- Init (config, strategy, state)
76:     |                    +-- Loop (dispatch, evaluate, decide)
77:     |                    +-- Synthesize (final research/research.md)
78:     |                    +-- Save (memory context)
79: ```

90: | Registry | `research/findings-registry.json` | JSON | Reducer-owned open/resolved questions and key findings |
91: | Dashboard | `research/deep-research-dashboard.md` | Markdown | Reducer-owned lifecycle and convergence summary |
92: | Iterations | `research/iterations/iteration-NNN.md` | Markdown | Per-iteration findings |
93: | Output | `research/research.md` | Markdown | Workflow-owned progressive synthesis output |

106: 
107: | Status | Meaning |
108: |--------|---------|
109: | `complete` | Normal iteration with findings |
110: | `timeout` | Exceeded time/tool budget |
111: | `error` | Failed to produce outputs |
112: | `stuck` | No new information found |
113: | `insight` | Low ratio but conceptual breakthrough |
114: | `thought` | Analytical-only, no evidence |
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## 7. CONVERGENCE DECISION TREE
119: 
120: ```text
121: Max iterations reached?
122:   Yes --> STOP
123: 
124: All questions answered?
125:   Yes --> STOP
126: 
127: stuckThreshold consecutive no-progress?
128:   Yes --> STUCK_RECOVERY
129:     Recovery works? --> CONTINUE
130:     Recovery fails? --> STOP (with gaps)
131: 
132: Composite convergence (3-signal weighted > 0.60)?
133:   Yes --> STOP (converged)
134: 
135: Otherwise --> CONTINUE
136: ```

139:

141: |--------|--------|---------------|-----------------|
142: | Rolling Average | 0.30 | 3 | avg(last 3 newInfoRatios) < convergenceThreshold |
143: | MAD Noise Floor | 0.35 | 4 | latest ratio <= MAD * 1.4826 |
144: | Question Entropy | 0.35 | 1 | answered / total questions >= 0.85 |
145: 
146: **Composite stop threshold:** 0.60 -- weighted stop score must exceed this before quality guards are evaluated.
147: 
148: Quality guards (source diversity, focus alignment, no single-weak-source) must pass before STOP.

151: 
152: ## 8. AGENT ITERATION CHECKLIST
153: 
154: Each @deep-research iteration:
155: 1. Read `deep-research-state.jsonl` and `deep-research-strategy.md`
156: 2. Determine focus from reducer-owned strategy "Next Focus"
157: 3. Execute 3-5 research actions (WebFetch, Grep, Read)
158: 4. Write `research/iterations/iteration-NNN.md` with findings
159: 5. Record the iteration through the append gateway, the only way a record reaches `deep-research-state.jsonl`

167: 
168: | Goal | Adjustment |
169: |------|------------|
170: | Deeper research | Lower convergence (0.02), raise max iterations (15) |
171: | Faster completion | Raise convergence (0.10), lower max iterations (5) |
172: | Broader coverage | Start with broad topic, let iterations narrow |
173: | Specific answer | Start with specific question, lower max iterations (5) |

180: |---------|-----|
181: | Stops too early | Lower `--convergence` from 0.05 to 0.02 |
182: | Repeats same research | Check strategy.md "Exhausted Approaches" is being read |
183: | Agent ignores state | Verify file paths in dispatch prompt |
184: | State file corrupt | Validate JSONL: `cat research/deep-research-state.jsonl \| jq .` |
185: | Loop runs too long | Set lower `--max-iterations` or higher `--convergence` |

210: Noise floor: 0.08 (ratio 0.10 ABOVE floor)
211: Stuck count: 0 | Segment: 1 | Recovery: none
212: Signals: RollingAvg=STOP MAD=CONTINUE Entropy=CONTINUE
213: ```

218: - In the convergence report (synthesis phase)
